summary.one_liner: composerize converts `docker run` commands into Docker Compose files and can merge them into an existing compose file.
summary.what_it_does: Takes a docker run command string and outputs equivalent compose.yaml content. It can be used from the command line after a global npm install, or imported as a Node.js module. Passing an existing compose file as a second argument merges the converted service into it. A third argument selects the target compose format: 'v2x', 'v3x', or 'latest' (Common Specification). A fourth argument sets the indentation level. The README also mentions a Docker image bundling the composerize, decomposerize and composeverter websites, and links to the reverse conversion (decomposerize) and a compose-format converter (composeverter).
use_cases: convert docker run command to docker-compose file
merge a docker run command into an existing compose file
generate compose config from node.js script
target a specific compose version (v2, v3, latest)
how_to_run: composerize docker run -p 80:80 -v /var/run/docker.sock:/tmp/docker.sock:ro --restart always --log-opt max-size=1g nginx
notable: Converts docker run flags into compose YAML, with optional merge into an existing compose file
Selectable output target: Compose v2.x, v3.x, or Common Specification
Adjustable indentation via a fourth function argument
Usable both as a global CLI and as a Node.js library
Companion tools referenced: decomposerize (reverse) and composeverter (compose format conversion)
caveats: README does not state limitations or unsupported docker run flags
Docker image is mentioned without details on its contents or maintenance
